name: Log4Shell JNDI injection attempt
description: A ${jndi:...} lookup string was written to the log. On servers running a vulnerable Log4j version (Minecraft 1.7-1.18.0) this makes the server fetch and execute attacker-controlled code.
recommendation: Update to Minecraft 1.18.1+ (or apply Mojang's Log4j patch), ban the player/IP, and check outbound connections from the server around this time.

name: Obfuscated Log4Shell payload
description: Nested Log4j lookups such as ${${lower:j}ndi:...} or ${${::-j}${::-n}di:...} are used to evade simple 'jndi' filters.
recommendation: Treat as a deliberate exploitation attempt: update Log4j, ban the source and review the server for compromise.

name: Operator / wildcard permission grant
description: A player ran a command that grants operator status or all permissions. If the player should not have this power, their account or a plugin may be compromised.
recommendation: Confirm the grant was authorised. Check ops.json and your permissions plugin, and rotate the account's password if unsure.

name: Sensitive administrative command
description: A player ran a command that weakens server protection (disabling the whitelist, unbanning, stopping the server, or changing gamerules that hide activity).
recommendation: Verify the player is a trusted admin and that the action was intended.

name: Mass destruction command
description: Commands that kill every entity/player or clear inventories are commonly used by griefers who have gained operator access.
recommendation: Check who gave this player permission and restore from backup if damage was done.

name: WorldEdit expression crash exploit
description: WorldEdit's //calc and //eval evaluate expressions; crafted expressions with huge loops have been used to freeze or crash servers.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1499 Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Deny the worldedit.calc permission to untrusted players and keep WorldEdit/FAWE updated.

name: Malformed / oversized packet
description: Errors such as oversized payloads, badly compressed packets or Netty decoder exceptions are typical of crash clients sending malicious packets.
pattern: Payload may not be larger than|Badly compressed packet|DecoderException|Packet too big|Book too large|exceeds the maximum allowed
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1499 Endpoint Denial of Service
recommendation: Identify the IP that sent the packet, block it, and consider an anti-exploit plugin or proxy.

name: Shell command injection attempt
description: Chat or command text contains shell syntax (pipes to a shell, command chaining, download-and-execute). Plugins that pass player input to the OS shell can be exploited this way.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter
recommendation: Audit plugins that run system commands, never pass player input to a shell, and ban the source.

name: Possible backdoor plugin trigger
description: Backdoored ('leaked' or cracked) plugins often listen for secret chat triggers such as '#op', '.console' or '!sudo' that give the sender operator or console access.
references: MITRE ATT&CK T1505 Server Software Component
recommendation: Check whether the player gained permissions straight after this message. Remove plugins not downloaded from official sources and scan jars with a tool such as MCAntiMalware.

name: IP logger / phishing link
description: Chat contains a link to a known IP-grabbing service or a URL shortener used to disguise malicious links.
recommendation: Delete the message if possible, warn players not to click it, and mute or ban the sender.

name: Server reconnaissance command
description: Listing plugins or the server version shows an attacker which vulnerable software is installed. Harmless on its own, but often the first step of an attack.
recommendation: Hide these commands from non-staff (e.g. revoke bukkit.command.plugins / bukkit.command.version).

name: Movement cheat detected by server
description: The server rejected impossible movement (flying, speed or teleport hacks), which indicates a modified client.
pattern: moved too quickly!|moved wrongly!|was kicked for floating too long|Flying is not enabled on this server
recommendation: Monitor the player and consider an anti-cheat plugin.

name: Session verification failure
description: A client failed Mojang session verification. This can be a network glitch, but repeated failures suggest a cracked client or an attempt to impersonate another player's username.
recommendation: Keep online-mode=true (or configure your proxy's forwarding secret correctly) and watch for repeats from the same IP.

name: Log / terminal escape injection
description: Raw ANSI escape sequences in the log can hide or rewrite lines when an admin views the log in a terminal, covering an attacker's tracks.
references: CWE-117 Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
recommendation: Filter control characters from chat and view logs with a tool that escapes them.
